name: Moving help
summary: Start a labor-only moving help business: your first 25 people and partner businesses, a price menu by home size from real ranges, quotes, a crew and hours estimate with a printable move-day plan, and a same-street route.

promises.same_street: One move's street turned into a route: door hangers with a neighbor price for a small job, a sheet for the 20 nearest homes and an intro ask for your customer.

items.item: Labor only, or a carrier with authority
items.what_to_check: Loading and unloading a truck the customer rents and drives is labor only. Driving a customer's goods for pay makes you a for-hire motor carrier; across state lines that takes a USDOT number and FMCSA operating authority before you start, plus the household goods rules in 49 CFR 375.

sources.says: For-hire motor carrier means a person engaged in the transportation of goods or passengers for compensation. Motor carriers file Form MCSA-1 to obtain a USDOT number and operating authority under 49 U.S.C. chapter 139, and may not begin operations until the USDOT number has been activated.

Part 375 applies when you transport household goods for individual shippers by motor vehicle in interstate commerce. A household goods motor carrier is a motor carrier that, in the course of transporting household goods, offers services such as loading and unloading at personal residences.

The MarketPlace Fee is a 15% fee collected from the total amount paid by a customer for a Moving Help service. All rates are based on hourly prices you set per crew size. The minimum a customer can reserve is 2 hours of service.

items.what_to_check: Many states license in-state movers. Florida defines a mover as anyone paid to load, carry or unload household goods as part of a household move, so a labor-only crew there may need to register ($300 a year) and keep liability insurance of at least $10,000 per shipment. California licenses movers through its Bureau of Household Goods and Services. Check your state.

sources.says: 507.01(9): Mover means a person who, for compensation, contracts for or engages in the loading, transportation or shipment, or unloading of household goods as part of a household move. 507.02(2): the chapter applies to moves that start and end in Florida. 507.03: movers register with the state; registration fees are $300 per year. 507.04: each mover keeps liability insurance of at least $10,000 per shipment (a mover with two or fewer vehicles may instead keep a $50,000 bond or certificate of deposit).

sources.publisher: NIOSH (CDC), Ergonomic Guidelines for Manual Material Handling, publication 2007-131
sources.says: The maximum weight to be lifted with two hands, under ideal conditions, is 51 pounds. Keep the load as close to the body as possible. Do not twist your body; step to one side or the other to turn. Team lifting: discuss your lifting plan so you don't make surprise movements. Wear appropriate shoes. Take rest breaks.

sources.publisher: OSHA, Materials Handling and Storage, publication 2236
sources.says: Workers should seek help when a load is so bulky it can't be properly grasped or lifted, when they can't see around or over it, or when they can't safely handle it. Protective equipment includes gloves, eye protection and steel-toed safety shoes or boots.

steps: Before the day: confirm both addresses, the date and start time, stairs and elevators at each end, where the truck parks, and any piano, safe or pool table.
On arrival: walk through with the customer, agree what goes and what stays, and photograph floors, door frames and anything already damaged.
Protect the path: runners on floors, jamb protectors on busy doorways, pads on banisters.
Pad and wrap furniture, take beds and tables apart, and bag and label the hardware.
Load in tiers, heaviest and strongest pieces at the base, and strap every 4 feet or so. Light boxes go over the cab.
Walk every room and closet with the customer before the truck leaves. The customer drives the truck.
Unload room by room, put beds and tables back together, walk through again with the customer, then send the invoice the same day.

sources.says: Protect floors on the heavy foot traffic paths with runners, plastic or cardboard; hook door jamb protectors around busy door frames or pad the furniture tightly; wrap banisters in pads. Old pads on floors bunch up and become a trip hazard.

Load in tiers with the heaviest and strongest items at the base, lighter as you go up; strap large furniture and appliances to the sides and strap off every four feet or so; keep the space over the cab for light items; finish with mattresses or tall pieces as a wall.

Estimating chart, load and unload: studio or small apartment 2 movers for 4 hours; 2 to 3 bedroom apartment 2 movers for 5 hours. Add 30 to 60 minutes for each set of stairs, and 30 minutes for pianos, pool tables and gun safes.

keep.referral: Hi {customer}, thanks again for trusting me with your {job}. If a friend or neighbor is moving soon, would you pass along my number{phone_part}? It means a lot to a new business.
keep.checkin: Hi {customer}, it's {first} from {business}. Hope the new place is coming together! If a heavy piece needs a new spot, just text me.
keep.card_ask: How did your move go? Scan to leave an honest review. Good or bad, it helps.
keep.rules: Ask every customer for a review, happy or not, and never offer a discount, gift or anything else for one; Google's rules forbid it. Only share photos the customer said yes to.

stairs.title: Extra flights of stairs (optional)
stairs.description: Flights past the first at each end, both ends added together. An elevator counts as a flight.

carry.title: Long carry, extra 75 foot stretches (optional)
carry.description: Past the first 150 feet from the truck to the door

heavy.title: Heavy items (optional)
heavy.description: Upright pianos, safes and pool tables

advice.say: A house this size usually takes 3 or 4 movers. Run "Crew and hours estimate" for the crew, the hours and a move-day plan.
Agree the list of pieces before the day. Past 2 hours, charge your hourly rate for each mover.
Say in writing who buys the boxes, tape and paper.
Heavy items: ask for the weight and the path out (steps, tight turns) before the day, and bring 3 movers and an appliance dolly. Grand pianos and hot tubs go to a specialist.

won.needs: the address, the new address, the stairs and elevator at each end, where the truck will park, and anything heavy like a piano or safe
prep_items: set aside anything flammable or under pressure, like gas cans, propane, paint and cleaners: movers can't carry them
empty and dry out the fridge, doors open 24 hours before
keep documents, medicine, jewelry and keys with you
save a parking spot for the truck close to the door, and book the elevator if there is one
bring: Two 4-wheel dollies and an appliance hand truck
Floor runners and door jamb protectors
Tool kit and bags for bed and table hardware
photos: Every room before you start, wide
Floors and door frames along the path, before and after
Any scratch or dent already there, close up, before you lift
The loaded truck before the door closes

proof.result: Padded, loaded and strapped in 3 hours, then unloaded room by room
proof.private: No faces, house numbers or street signs.

street.headline: One heavy piece moved free on {street}
includes: A couch, dresser or bookcase moved to a new room
how: Text me your address or scan the code
We stop by while we're on {street}{day_part}
Point to the piece and where it goes
street.line: We're helping with a move on {street}{day_part}, so the first 3 neighbors who text me get one heavy piece moved inside their home free: about 15 minutes, no cost and no catch.
street.post: Hi neighbors! I'm {first}, I run {business} here in {area}. We're helping with a move on {street}{day_part}, so the first 3 neighbors who text me get one heavy piece moved inside their home free (about 15 minutes). No cost and no catch. {phone_line}
steps: Hang the door hangers on {street} the day before, on the door, never in or on a mailbox.
Move the first 3 pieces for neighbors who text, two of you, after the paid job.
Hand them the card with your price before you leave.
Text a thank-you the same day, then one follow-up in 3 days.

realtors.demo: staging furniture moved at one of your listings, free, up to an hour with 2 movers
realtors.headline: Careful hands for moving day
realtors.card_line: Buying or selling with {biz}? Mention them when you book.
steps: Send the message and the card today, with two days you can do it.
Do the sample with a second mover on the day the agent picks. Take photos before and after, with no house numbers.
Send the photos to the agent the same day.
Ask once: would they leave your cards with buyers and sellers who are moving?

apartments.demo: one free hour with 2 movers for a resident your office picks, to load a truck or move furniture
apartments.headline: Moving in or out? We do the heavy lifting
apartments.card_line: Live at {biz}? Mention it when you book.
steps: Walk in with the card and ask for the property manager.
Offer the free hour for one resident they pick, on a day that suits the office.
Send the office a photo of the work the same day, with no faces or unit numbers.
Ask once: could they leave your cards at the leasing office for residents who are moving?

self_storage.demo: one unit loaded or unloaded free for a renter you pick, up to an hour with 2 movers
self_storage.headline: Your unit loaded tight and stacked safe
self_storage.card_line: Renting at {biz}? Mention it when you book.
steps: Walk in with the card and ask for the manager.
Offer to load or unload one unit free for a renter they pick.
Stack heavy boxes low, leave an aisle, then send the manager a photo.
Ask once: could they keep your cards at the counter or pin one on their board?

senior_living.demo: one resident's furniture moved or rearranged free, up to an hour with 2 movers, on a day your staff picks
senior_living.headline: Careful moving help for move-in day
senior_living.card_line: Moving into {biz}? Mention it when you book.
steps: Call or walk in and ask for the move-in coordinator or the director.
Offer the free hour for one resident they pick, with family there if they want.
Pad corners and walls, place each piece where the resident wants it, and take nothing away without a yes.
Ask once: could they share your card with families planning a move-in?

truck_rental.demo: an hour of free loading help with 2 movers for one of your renters
truck_rental.headline: You drive. We load it tight and strapped.
truck_rental.card_line: Renting a truck at {biz}? Mention it when you book.
steps: Walk in on a weekday morning, when the counter is quiet, and ask for the manager.
Offer an hour of free loading help for one renter they send your way.
Load heavy pieces first, in tiers, and strap every 4 feet or so. The renter drives.
Ask once: could they keep your cards at the counter for renters who need loading help?

same_street.neighbor_note: judgment call, not a sourced fact
same_street.headline: Your neighbor price on {street}
includes: Furniture moved or rearranged in the home
A storage unit or container loaded
how: Text me your address or scan the code
We come while we're on {street}{day_part}, or a day that suits you
same_street.customer_ask: Hi {customer}, thanks again for trusting us with your move! If a neighbor ever needs a hand with heavy furniture or a move, would you pass on my number{phone_part}? It means a lot to a new business.
steps: Hang a door hanger on every home on this sheet the day of the move or the day before. On the door, never in or on a mailbox.
Park the truck so it doesn't block a neighbor's driveway, and keep the sidewalk clear.
If a neighbor is outside, say hi and keep it short. Never say whose move it is: "We're helping with a move on your street."
Text your customer the intro ask after the job, never before.
same_street.why: Neighbors see the crew at work on moving day, and a small job on the same street means no extra drive, so they get a better price.
